survivors.claim: `policy-check --json` and `generate --dry-run` print their machine-consumed payload with `console.log(...)` immediately followed by `process.exit(...)` — the exact shape the host rules § Gotchas names as truncating at the 64 KiB pipe buffer while still exiting 0. Today's payloads are tiny (a handful of finding strings / a few dozen `  + ` lines) so no truncation is reachable, which is why this is advisory, not hard.
survivors.impact: If a future host ever produces a very long drift list or file list, the doctor check or init confirm could read a cut-off payload while the exit code still says success.
survivors.evidence: spec/scripts/init-gen.js:193-196 `if (asJson) console.log(JSON.stringify(findings)) ... process.exit(findings.length ? 1 : 0)`; :735-738 `console.log(`Confirm before writing: ...`) ... process.exit(0)`. Rules § Gotchas: "Any script that prints a payload and exits routes through a synchronous writer (`fs.writeSync` on fd 1 ...)". Not executed as a defect — payload sizes here cannot reach 64 KiB on any realistic host.

survivors.claim: When the host config carries no string `pipelineRules`, `policy-check` sets `rulesRel = ''`, so `path.join(root, '')` reads the root directory (EISDIR, swallowed) and every `riskTiers` entry is reported as `not in  § Risk Tiers` with an empty filename — the finding names no file to fix. The contract requires `pipelineRules`, so this only bites a hand-broken config; a one-line fallback naming the missing key would make the message self-remedying.
survivors.impact: An owner whose config lost its rules-file key would see risk-area warnings that point at a blank filename instead of at the real problem.
survivors.evidence: spec/scripts/init-gen.js:184 `const rulesRel = typeof cfg.pipelineRules === 'string' ? cfg.pipelineRules : ''`; :186 `path.join(root, rulesRel)` with `catch { /* absent rules file: every entry is reported */ }`; :188 message template. Read from source; not reachable through any spec'd path (grounding-contract § Required config keys requires `pipelineRules`).
